core_obligations: Set up the finite order thickening and its nilpotent ideal.
Filter F by powers of the ideal and identify the graded pieces.
Kill H^1 of each piece via affineness of X.
Induct on the filtration to conclude with Serre's criterion.

proof_roadmap.step: Graded pieces are pushforwards from X.
Cohomology comparison on X' vs X.

difficulty_reason: The lemma (with the chapter's slogan 'Affineness is insensitive to thickenings') states that any thickening of an affine scheme is affine, citing EGA1 Proposition 5.1.9 for the finite-order case. Two retained proofs are collected: the short pointer proof (special case of Limits, proposition affine, quoted by name) and the substantive proof for a finite order thickening — the latter is written out in the retained span: given X ⊂ X' finite order with X affine, Serre's criterion (Cohomology of Schemes, lemma quasi-compact-h1-zero-covering) reduces affineness of X' to vanishing H^1 for quasi-coherent F; the nilpotent ideal I = Ker(O_{X'} -> i_*O_X) gives the filtration F_a = I^a F whose successive quotients are i_*G_a pushforwards from X (Morphisms, lemma i-star-equivalence), whose H^1 on X' equals H^1 on X (Cohomology of Schemes, lemma relative-affine-cohomology) and vanishes by affineness of X (Cohomology of Schemes, lemma quasi-coherent-affine-cohomology-zero); a finite induction concludes. The general case then rests on the collected pointer to the Limits proposition. Retained author spans: statement 156-165, proofs 167-170 and 172-206.

dedup.scope: Affineness of an arbitrary thickening of an affine scheme, with the finite-order Serre-criterion proof.
